Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

affect verb

have an effect on

also be affected, be affected by, move (the feelings), be moved, be deeply affected, be upset by, all shook up, shaken up

classical

Cic. Fam. 16.4.1: variē sum adfectus tuīs litterīs
Liv. 28.15: famēs sitisque corpora adficerent (Lewis & Short)

afficiō, afficere, affēcī, affectum

verb, third conjugation (-iō): with the accusative, often with an ablative of the state produced

affect, act on (body or mind)

Lewis & Short: “to do something to one, i.e. to exert an influence on body or mind, so that it is brought into such or such a state”. Passive: be affected, often with an ablative: dolōre afficī, to feel pain (Traupman 105, 152); morbō affectus, ill. Where “affect” means “concern, apply to”, see concern (be about, matter to): attinet, pertinet ad.

Other words

  • commoveō, commovēre, commōvī, commōtum — move deeply, shake, upset

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 3.10.1: graviter prīmō nūntiō commōtus sum; Cic. Fam. 12.19.2: sānē mē commōvit

    Of news and events that disturb the mind; Augustine uses it of being moved to tears.

  • moveō, movēre, mōvī, mōtum — move, touch (the feelings)

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.6.4: verbīs nōn moveor tuīs

Examples

  • Variē sum adfectus tuīs litterīs, valdē priōre pāginā perturbātus, paulum alterā recreātus.

    Your letter affected me in two ways: the first page upset me badly, the second cheered me up a little.Cic. Fam. 16.4.1

  • etsī graviter prīmō nūntiō commōtus sum

    although I was badly shaken by the first newsCic. Fam. 3.10.1

  • quantum flēvī in hymnīs et canticīs tuīs, suāve sonantis ecclēsiae tuae vōcibus commōtus ācriter!

    how I wept at your hymns and songs, deeply moved by the voices of your sweetly singing church!Aug. Conf. 9.6.14

  • Vehementer perturbātus sum.

    I’m all shook up.Traupman 107

See also effect, concern, feel.
